dome.name: Dome generator
dome.notice: A drawing, take-off and first-analysis aid. It is not a structural design: the forces are linear elastic theory for an uncracked shell under simple load patterns, and nothing here is checked against your site or your local code. A licensed engineer must design and check the dome, and the local authority decides what may be built.
dome.shape.help: The diameter and the height are those of the inflated form (the outside of the foam). Foam and concrete are sprayed on its inside, so the clear inside is smaller: the result gives it. A stem wall is a straight wall under the curve, so the dome starts higher above the ground.
dome.governed.help: Leave a box empty and the generator fills it: from the spec you picked when it has a value, otherwise from a starting figure. Starting figures are not from any standard. Type your own figure to overrule either.
dome.o.help: An opening is cut between two straight sides that point at the centre, from its sill up to its head. Its width is true on the form's face at the sill. The angle is where it stands round the dome, counter-clockwise from the right-hand side of the plan (0°).
dome.loads.help: These feed the forces only. Snow, wind and earthquake are yours to set from your loads standard and your engineer: leave one at 0 and that case is left out. Wind is a pressure; earthquake is the sideways force as a share of the weight (0.2 = a fifth). The stiffness and the buckling reduction are your engineer's figures too.
dome.forces.notice: Linear elastic theory for an uncracked shell. The first tables are membrane theory; bending follows below for loads that are the same all the way round. Not covered: bending under wind or earthquake, uneven snow, temperature, shrinkage, cracking and creep. These are figures for your engineer to start from, not a design. Minus is compression, plus is tension.
dome.f.name: Name
dome.f.cover: Cover to steel in the shell
dome.f.steelStress: Steel stress for the steel areas (your figure)
dome.f.headroom: Headroom to measure the usable floor
dome.opt.shape.sphere: Part of a sphere (up to a half sphere)
dome.from.start: starting figure, not from a standard
dome.read.secondary: read in a document that quotes the standard, not the standard itself
dome.spec.label: Spec in force
dome.spec.pick: Pick the spec the dome is designed to. Its values fill the empty boxes and the design is checked against the ones it holds as numbers. The other rules are shown for you and your engineer to read.
dome.spec.add: No spec add-on is switched on. Add “Dome spec: United States” or “Dome spec: Europe” from the Library (Settings, Add-ons) to bring norm values in. Until then every figure is yours or a starting figure.
dome.spec.counts: This spec holds {primary} rules read in the standards themselves, {secondary} read in documents that quote them, and {none} with no value we could read. Check every value against your own copy of the standard, its current edition and your local amendments.
dome.spec.nonecheck: No spec in force: nothing was checked against a norm.
dome.check.none: Nothing in this design breaks a value the spec holds. That is not a design check.
dome.err.range: Out of range ({lo} to {hi}); the default is used.
dome.err.choice: Not one of the choices; the default is used.
dome.err.sphere: Part of a sphere cannot be taller than half the diameter ({hi} mm); it was set to that. Choose half an ellipse for a taller dome.
dome.err.tall: Taller than twice the diameter; it was set to {hi} mm.
dome.err.flat: Flatter than a twentieth of the diameter; it was set to {lo} mm.
dome.err.opening: Opening {n} was left out: {part} must be between {lo} and {hi}.
dome.err.many: Only the first {hi} openings are used.
dome.rule.shell.cover.min: Cover to steel in the shell, at least
dome.rule.footing.cover.min.earth: Cover to steel against earth, at least
dome.rule.shell.rebar.ratio.min: Steel ratio in the shell, at least
dome.rule.steel.yield: Yield strength of the usual bar
dome.rule.shell.rebar.spacing.rule: Bar spacing, as the code words it
dome.rule.shell.rebar.layers: One layer of steel or two
dome.rule.shell.analysis: How a shell may be analysed
dome.rule.load.standard: Where snow, wind and earthquake loads come from
dome.act.ifc.done: Saved the dome as an IFC4 file.
dome.act.csv.done: Saved the figures, quantities and forces.
dome.issue.below: {what}: {value} {unit} is below the spec's minimum of {limit} {unit}
dome.issue.above: {what}: {value} {unit} is above the spec's figure of {limit} {unit}
dome.issue.note: {what}: the spec's limit is {limit} {unit} (not checked by the generator)
dome.problem.opening.high: Opening {n} reaches {head} mm, too close to the crown (at most {top} mm); it was left out.
dome.problem.opening.wide: Opening {n} is too wide for the dome at its sill; it was left out.
dome.problem.opening.overlap: Opening {n} overlaps another opening; it was left out.
dome.problem.shell.thin: A {shell} mm shell leaves little room for steel with {cover} mm of cover on each face.
dome.problem.footing.narrow: The ring beam ({footing} mm) is narrower than the concrete standing on it ({base} mm).
dome.problem.footing.wide: The ring beam is wider than the dome's radius allows; no floor slab was made.
dome.problem.headroom.none: The clear height at the centre ({clear} mm) is below the headroom asked ({headroom} mm).
dome.problem.stress.high: The largest membrane compression ({stress} MPa, unfactored) is above the concrete strength ({strength} MPa).
dome.fc.load: Load of the dome carried at the springline
dome.fc.nohoop: none: the shell stays in compression
dome.fc.ring: Tension in the ring at the springline
dome.fc.bearing: Pressure under the ring beam (dome, stem wall and beam)
dome.fc.ringsteel: Steel area for the ring tension
dome.fc.hoopsteel: Steel area for the largest tension round the dome
dome.q.steel: Steel in shell, stem wall and ring beam
dome.q.inside.headroom: Floor area with the headroom asked
dome.report.title: Dome
dome.bim.note: Place in the model writes the dome into the open model on its first level, as elements you can select, schedule and save in the IFC file. One step that Undo takes back; placing again replaces the dome of the same name.
dome.bim.nolevel: The model has no level to stand the dome on. Open or start a model first.
dome.bim.place.label: place the dome
dome.bim.remove.label: remove the dome
dome.bim.none: No dome of this name is in the model.
dome.cad.note: Draw plan and section puts the dome into the drawing as circles, arcs, polylines, text and dimensions on DOME- layers. One step that Undo takes back. The lines do not follow later changes: remove and draw again. The IFC file is the 3D model.
dome.cad.draw.label: draw the dome
dome.cad.remove.label: remove the dome drawing
dome.cad.none: Nothing on a DOME- layer to remove.
dome.factors.help: Load factors multiply each load before the forces are worked out. With no spec they are 1 and the forces are unfactored. A spec side add-on fills them from its code; type your own to overrule it.
dome.frame.help: A frame is a band of thicker concrete round every opening: at each side, over the head and under the sill. Leave either box at 0 for none.
dome.forces.unfactored: Unfactored: every load factor is 1. Pick a spec, or type the factors under Load factors, for factored forces.
dome.forces.factored: Factored: own weight alone × {alone}; with other loads × {dead} (× {min} where it helps); snow × {snow}; wind × {wind}; earthquake × {seismic}.
dome.opt.baseFix.ring: Free to spread against the ring beam
dome.f.seismic: Earthquake, share of the weight sideways (your figure)
dome.f.gammaDead: Factor on own weight, with other loads
dome.f.gammaDeadMin: Factor on own weight where it helps
dome.rule.load.factor.dead: Factor on own weight, with other loads
dome.rule.load.factor.dead.min: Factor on own weight where it helps
dome.rule.load.factor.snow.accompanying: Factor on snow when wind leads
dome.rule.snow.dome: Snow on domes and curved roofs
dome.lat.wind: The textbook wind pattern: your pressure on the windward side at the base, fading to nothing over the crown and to the same suction on the leeward side. Codes put more suction over the crown: use your code's coefficients for the real design. Amplitudes: each force is largest on the windward and leeward lines, the shear at the sides.
dome.lat.seismic: A sideways force of your share of the dome's own weight, everywhere at once. No dynamic analysis, no ground or soil effect. Amplitudes: each force is largest on the line of the push, the shear at the sides.
dome.lat.floor: Vertical force at the floor from this load alone
dome.lat.floormax: With the least own weight, at the floor
dome.lat.floormin: With the most own weight, at the floor
dome.lat.uplift: uplift: the base must be anchored
dome.lat.along: Along the curve, most tension / most compression
dome.lat.round: Round the dome, most tension / most compression
dome.lat.upsteel: Steel area to hold the uplift
dome.b.notice: The shell solved with its bending, base: {base}. This is where the moments at the ring beam, at the top of a stem wall and where the thickness changes come from. Loads that are the same all the way round only. Uncracked concrete: a cracked shell is softer and moves more. Plus is tension; a plus moment stretches the inside face.
dome.b.push: Outward push on the ring beam
dome.b.notension: none: every face stays in compression
dome.bk.notice: The pressure a perfect elastic shell of this curvature and thickness would buckle at, against the load pressing on it. Real concrete shells buckle far below that figure, because of imperfections, creep and cracking. The reduction is your engineer's: type it and the last row shows the margin that is left.
dome.bk.pressure: Load pressing on the shell there
dome.bk.noreduce: no reduction typed: not a margin yet
dome.of.notice: What the membrane forces would have carried through each opening, under the heavier of the cases that are the same all the way round. The frame and its steel must take them round: this is the size of that job, not its design. Bending round the opening is not calculated.
dome.of.along: Along the curve, over the head ({u})
dome.of.round: Round the dome, cut by the height ({u})
dome.q.bars.length: Bars in the shell, both ways
dome.q.nolaps: no laps, no ring beam cage
dome.bars.ratio: Your bars give a steel ratio of {crown} at the crown and {base} at the base each way; the ratio asked is {want}.
dome.problem.bending.failed: The bending could not be solved for this shape.
dome.problem.uplift.wind: Wind lifts the base on the windward side by {n} kN/m with the least own weight: the base must be anchored.
dome.problem.uplift.seismic: The earthquake force lifts the base on one side by {n} kN/m with the least own weight: the base must be anchored.
dome.problem.buckling.low: With your reduction the classical buckling pressure is only {ratio} times the load: below 1.
dome.problem.bars.light: Your bars give a steel ratio of {have} at the base, below the {want} asked.
dome.problem.stress.bending: The largest compression with bending ({stress} MPa) is above the concrete strength ({strength} MPa).
dome.forces.legend: In the tables: Angle is measured from the crown; Along is the force along the curve from crown to base; Round is the force round the dome; σ is a stress; M is a bending moment; Height is above the floor.
